spec: docs/DECOY-ACCOUNT.md §1, §7 — PYROVLT1 container, one 2 MiB half sealed
description: Cross-platform container test vector. Both platforms build a container from these inputs and must produce container.sha256 exactly. No container file is checked in: one is 12,582,925 bytes of mostly incompressible padding, and four of them across two platforms is fifty megabytes of test data that compresses to nothing.

byteSource.note: A platform RNG cannot be the source: SecRandomCopyBytes and java.util.Random are different streams. This counter construction is the same three lines in either language.
byteSource.construction: stream(seed, n): out = "", ctr = 0; while len(out) < n: out += SHA-256(seed(32 bytes) || ctr(4 bytes, big-endian)); ctr += 1; return out[:n]
byteSource.continuity: ONE stream per container. The counter runs on across every request and does NOT restart per call; a request that is not a multiple of 32 keeps the remainder for the next request.
drawOrder: 1. padding of the sealed half: halfCapacity - seqBytes - lengthBytes - payload.bytes = 2096955
2. nonce of the sealed half: 12 bytes
3. every remaining half, in increasing FILE OFFSET, 2097152 bytes each (5 halves here)

payload.note: Sealed VERBATIM, as these exact UTF-8 bytes. Never re-encode it through a JSON encoder: neither platform fixes dictionary key order, which is why §7 says byte-identity is unreachable for ordinary saves. It is a valid Blob, so the vector also proves the container holds something the app can read.

layout.halfPlaintext: seq(8, big-endian) || length(4, big-endian) || JSON(Blob) || random padding
